t: The Signature Vision: Zero-Waste Circular Cities
title: The Signature Vision: Zero-Waste Circular Cities
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Zero-Waste Circular Cities.
description:

Signature loop hulls program, charter one: master sorting districts at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale material transit manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate industrial symbiosis systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Zero-Waste Circular Cities becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

t: 2030 — The first loop hulls district opens at 50
title: 2030 — The first loop hulls district opens at 50
definition: 2030 milestone on the Zero-Waste Circular Cities roadmap.
description:
The first loop hulls district opens at 50,000 residents, its sorting districts grid and material transit mobility running at full design load.

What must be true first: the sorting districts results have to replicate outside the lab, material transit manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and industrial symbiosis operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed sorting districts demonstrations, material transit cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting industrial symbiosis uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Zero-Waste Circular Cities
definition: Estimates Zero-Waste Circular Cities readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Zero-Waste Circular Cities components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a loop hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

definition: Simulates Zero-Waste Circular Cities operating for a day.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where sorting districts monitoring, material transit redundancy, or industrial symbiosis maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Zero-Waste Circular Cities Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Zero-Waste Circular Cities: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Zero-Waste Circular Cities — cities where every output becomes another's input.

Phase 1 — Prove (sorting districts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (material transit): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (industrial symbiosis): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (repair blocks): loop hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and urban core-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
